_why: Every mutation receipt pins the WHOLE-FILE sha256 of five runner components. That
makes any edit to the runner -- a comment, a docstring, a new function -- void every
receipt in the repository at once. Measured 2026-08-30: appending one comment line to
conductor/mutation_testing.py dropped coverage from 505 to 74, with 431 test paths
rejected for 'runner hash mismatch, runner component hash map mismatch'.
That is the same over-broad-pin pathology the per-symbol source pins exist to fix,
one level up: a content pin over an entire file where only a narrow semantic surface
determines what a receipt MEANS.
This file narrows it. An entry declares that receipts produced by the runner at the
recorded hashes are semantically equivalent to receipts produced by the current
runner, because the diff between them does not change how any mutant is applied,
how any outcome is decided, or what any receipt field means.
This is NOT a bypass and NOT the frozen legacy v2 git anchor, which stays frozen:
- it rewrites no receipt -- the 'refuses to write a receipt it did not regenerate'
rule is untouched;
- every entry names its justification and the exact diff it covers;
- deleting an entry restores strict whole-file behaviour immediately;
- an entry is only added after a SAMPLE of campaigns has been re-run under both
runners and shown to produce identical outcomes. Proven, never asserted.
Do NOT add an entry for a change that alters mutant application, outcome
classification, receipt field semantics, or scope validation. Those receipts are
genuinely stale and must be regenerated by re-running their campaigns.

entries.justification: Runner state on master immediately before repin_campaigns gained two refusals and three helpers moved into the support module. Every change is confined to `repin`, the re-pinning CLI: it selects campaigns, rewrites manifest pins and chooses a receipt path. It does not decide any mutant's outcome. Mutant application (apply_mutation), scoring, ranking, killer attribution, scope validation and receipt CONTENT (run_campaign, which writes every field) are byte-identical to master. The one receipt-adjacent change is which directory `repin --run` hands run_campaign as its output path -- previously a gitignored `research/reports/` fallback, now the registry's declared receipt directory -- which changes where a receipt lands, not what any receipt field means. A receipt produced under the recorded hash-set therefore describes the same run the new runner would produce.

entries.justification: Runner state on master (d06d4ba6e) immediately before repin learned to check what the gate actually checks. Two changes. First, `conductor/mutation_campaign_model.py` is a new module holding the campaign dataclasses, the sha256 helpers, `_runner_components_sha256`, `_lineage_accepts`, `symbol_hashes`, `source_drift`, `_campaign_receipts` and `_load_registry`, all moved VERBATIM out of `mutation_testing.py` (1,351 -> 1,177 lines), which re-exports every name it moved. Second, `receipt_drift` is new: it runs the gate's own acceptance predicate over each campaign's receipts and reports the campaigns whose receipts the gate would reject. Neither touches mutant application, scoring, ranking, killer attribution, scope validation, or any receipt field: `apply_mutation` and `run_campaign` are byte-identical to master. A receipt produced under the recorded hash-set therefore describes the same run the new runner would produce, and the new module is in RUNNER_COMPONENT_PATHS (8 -> 9 files) only so that a future edit to the moved code invalidates receipts the way an edit to its old home did.

entries.justification: Runner state on master (7752a0ab7) immediately before the anchored patch applier was added BEHIND `git apply`, as a fallback. `git apply --check` still runs first and still decides every patch it can apply, byte for byte, by the same code that produced every receipt in this repository. The anchored applier is consulted only where git REFUSED -- and a refusal used to abort the whole campaign before any mutant executed, so no receipt can exist for a patch that reaches the new code, and no outcome any receipt already records can change. Mutant application, outcome classification, killer attribution, receipt field semantics and scope validation are untouched. Measured, not asserted: a differential over all 3,416 registered mutants applied each patch under both paths -- 3,313 apply byte-identically, ZERO disagree, 74 are refused by both, 5 have no patch file on disk, and 24 that `git apply` had retired come back. Each of those 24 belongs to a campaign that could not run at all under the old runner, so none of them contradicts a recorded outcome. The new module is in RUNNER_COMPONENT_PATHS (9 -> 10) so that a future edit to it invalidates receipts the way an edit to the runner's other components does.

entries.justification: Runner state on master (e91fb4df5) immediately before run_campaign was split into five named stages and the receipt-building half moved into a new module. run_campaign had cyclomatic complexity 40 across 178 lines, which is the finding this change answers; nothing about what the runner DECIDES was touched. Six symbols moved from conductor/mutation_testing.py to the new conductor/mutation_receipt_build.py with byte-identical ASTs -- _BARE_INTERPRETERS, _utc_stamp, _pin_interpreter, _torch_version, killer_enforcement and _default_receipt_path -- and three more (_resolve_receipt_path, _open_receipt, _score_receipt) were lifted out of run_campaign's body, so those three are a genuine refactor and NOT a move: their equivalence is measured below, not asserted. Snapshot isolation, manifest and patch hash binding, mutant application, outcome classification, killer attribution, receipt field semantics, scope validation and receipt registration are unchanged. The new module is in RUNNER_COMPONENT_PATHS (10 -> 11) so that a future edit to the receipt builder invalidates receipts exactly as an edit to the runner's other components does; that addition is what makes this entry necessary, because it re-pins the map every existing receipt carries.
